title: Forensic snapshot & replay PRD (private deployments)
content:
Purpose / brief
- Sketch PRD for a forensic snapshot + replay facility for Private deployments (VPC / on-prem).
- Goal: provide a tamper-evident, queryable package of the state and traffic necessary to reconstruct a customer environment interaction for audits, post-incident analysis, and approval-gate validation.

Context / why now
- Customers ask for stronger evidence trails when we perform control-plane changes or when they ask us to validate networking/egress behavior.
- Existing audit logs capture events but are fragmented (operator UI, control-plane events, RPC logs, and agent telemetry). Reconstructing a sequence of events is time-consuming and error-prone.
- Need a product-grade capability that: (a) collects coherent snapshots tied to approval decisions, (b) attaches cryptographic attestation, (c) supports replay in a sandbox for investigation.

Primary users / personas
- Customer security engineer: requests evidence for compliance and needs a packaged artifact to send to auditors.
- Redwood SRE/Incident responder: needs to reproduce customer-reported failures to diagnose root cause.
- Product compliance reviewer: verifies approval-gate enforcement during tenant network changes.

Non-goals
- Not a full traffic capture/packet store for long-term packet-level retention. We’ll integrate with packet capture partners or existing customer tooling where required.
- Not intended as a general-purpose backup/restore system for customer data.

User stories
- As a customer security engineer, I can request a forensic snapshot anchored to a specific approval event and download a signed artifact I can hand to auditors.
- As an SRE, I can request a replay of the snapshot in an isolated sandbox with synthetic ingress to reproduce a failure.
- As a product reviewer, I can see which approval gates were evaluated, the inputs provided, and the resulting decision artifacts.

Functional requirements (high level)
1) Snapshot composition
   - Control plane events: approval decision record, operator id, timestamp, and related metadata (request id, route, model variant, etc.).
   - Agent telemetry: sequence of relevant agent logs (bounded window around event, configurable 5–30 min default).
   - Networking state: VPC route table snapshot (customer-provided), peering/IDS flags, egress config (not raw packet capture), and NAT/Gateway change events.
   - Routing & policy decisions: policy evaluation traces for any approval gate that evaluated the change.
   - Config diffs: pre-change and post-change manifest for relevant resources.
   - Minimal sample of application-level requests (tokenized, redacted by default) to reproduce request semantics - preserve PII redaction policy.
   - Evidence metadata: sequence hash, snapshot id (UUID), signing root, retention metadata, and hash chain pointer to the approval event.

2) Attestation / tamper-evidence
   - Every snapshot MUST be signed by a Redwood attestation key (customer-managed signing option for Private deployments where customer wants the signing key).
   - Include an append-only digest chain linking approval events -> snapshot(s) -> replay result artifacts.
   - Signed manifest must include operator identity, approval gate name and version, and environment fingerprint (cluster id, agent versions).

3) Storage & retention
   - Snapshots stored encrypted-at-rest in customer-approved storage (for Private: customer S3/GCS, or on-prem vault path).
   - Retention policy configurable per-customer (default 90d for Private).
   - Metadata index retained in control plane for quick search (index stores only hashes and non-sensitive keys).

4) Querying & discovery
   - API: list-snapshots(customer_id, filter_by_event, time-range, approval-id).
   - Support for export: download-snapshot(snapshot_id, include-logs: bool).
   - Minimal UI in Console: timeline view tied to approval gate history with quick links to snapshot download / request replay.

5) Replay sandbox
   - Replay target is an isolated Fargate/GKE sandbox with synthetic inputs that simulate external calls and internal ingress.
   - Replays run with strict resource/time limits; produce a replay report and link back to original snapshot id.
   - Replays are ephemeral; outputs are attached as a replay artifact (signed) and stored according to short retention (14 days by default).

6) Approval gate integration
   - When an approval is triggered for a customer-managed network change, create an automatic snapshot pre-change and (on acceptance) post-change.
   - Approval records must reference snapshot ids. Snapshot creation is an approval step plugin with a timeout and fallback (if snapshot creation fails, approval should either block or require manual override — configurable by tenancy).

7) Security & privacy
   - Default redaction rules: mask tokens, API keys, PII per our redact engine. Customer may provide allowlist of fields to preserve in Private deployments (requires signed agreement).
   - Audit of who downloaded snapshot artifacts with token-level audit logs.

APIs (sketch)
- POST /v1/private/snapshots?approval_id=<id>&type=pre|post&window=10m  -> starts snapshot job, returns snapshot_id
- GET  /v1/private/snapshots/<snapshot_id>  -> metadata + signed manifest
- GET  /v1/private/snapshots/<snapshot_id>/download?include_logs=true  -> presigned URL (customer storage) or streamed archive
- POST /v1/private/snapshots/<snapshot_id>/replay -> queue replay job, returns replay_id
- GET  /v1/private/replays/<replay_id> -> replay status + artifacts

Console UX notes
- Approval timeline card: approval entry expands to show pre/post snapshot ids, signed digest, small summary (operator, gate, decision and link to download).
- Snapshot viewer: high-level manifest and redaction summary. Full download behind an extra confirmation modal ("This may contain sensitive data").

Operational concerns / infra notes
- Snapshot creation must be rate-limited per-tenant. Large snapshots (over X MB) should be streamed directly to customer storage to avoid control-plane OOM.
- We need an agent-side bundler that understands local network/state and can produce a normalized manifest. Agent must tag snapshots with agent-version and include provenance headers.
- For replay, sandbox infra must support multiple runtime images (we need Python/http client harness + small LLM runtime shim).

Rollout plan (phased)
- Phase 0 (alpha): internal-only snapshots for a few Security/SE customers. Manual processes for handoff and manual signing.
- Phase 1 (beta_partner): add attestation signing, console UI, and replay sandbox; test with 2 pilot customers (one VPC, one on-prem).
- Phase 2 (general-availability): enable customer-managed signing keys, retention SLA, and automation around approval gating.

Metrics / success criteria
- Time to produce snapshot (target: < 90s 90th percentile for small snapshots).
- % of approvals that have an associated pre/post snapshot (target: 95% in enabled tenants).
- Mean time to reproduce incident using snapshot + replay (target: 50% reduction vs manual).

Risks & mitigations
- Privacy leak risk: default aggressive redaction and require explicit customer opt-in to include unredacted samples.
- Storage cost blowup: streaming to customer-owned buckets and size warnings in Console.
- Approval-flow deadlocks if snapshot creation fails: allow configurable fallback to manual override + operator notification.

Open questions
- What is the canonical snapshot size limit before we switch to streaming? (engineering input needed)
- Customer-managed signing: do we provide a lightweight KMS adaptor for on-prem HSMs or require key import?
- Replay fidelity expectations: do we capture exact network timing or only logical request ordering?

Next steps / immediate TODOs
- Engineering spike: implement an agent bundler prototype and measure snapshot size distribution across pilot tenants (assigned: Devon).
- Security review: threat model for snapshot artifacts and attestation flows (assigned: Sofia).
- Legal: checklist for customer opt-in language for PII retention in snapshots (assigned: Priya).
- Create Jira epic and link to this doc (JIRA-1427 currently created as placeholder).

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally a sketch to capture product boundary and main failure modes. Looking for input on: attachment format (tar.gz vs zstd chunked), signing key model for on-prem, and replay infra sizing.
- Prefer feedback inline in the doc or via the JIRA-1427 thread.

-- end of sketch --
